findings.text: Start from your team's actual bottleneck, not the feature list. If double bookings are the problem, test collective or round-robin scheduling directly by blocking a calendar and trying to book through it. If manual CRM entry is the problem, check whether Salesforce or HubSpot sync is included at your plan tier or reserved for a higher one. If you're a telehealth or healthcare team, confirm compliance coverage like HIPAA alignment before you scale, since that's often an add-on tier rather than a default . And if Google Calendar or Outlook is your team's daily driver, verify the sync depth (one-way versus two-way, and how many calendars per user) rather than assuming every "calendar integration" claim behaves the same way; a closer look at how these programs compare against Google Calendar's own scheduling tools is worth the ten minutes it takes. Whichever program you land on, the fastest way to confirm it fits is the same for every vendor: create the accounts, block a calendar, and try to break it before you pay for it.
